result.summary:
Independently re-verified ISS-0397's resolution end-to-end rather than trusting the chain of PASSes. (1) Original symptom: re-read ISS-0397.yaml's description (Engine.build_instance_state/3 hardcoded join_counters: %{} on every call, so a PARALLEL_GATEWAY join could only fire within the same hop-chain as its own split) and read the real concurrent regression test directly: test/letflow/iss0397_join_counters_test.exs, describe 'concurrent sibling-branch completion: two Task.async complete_task/3 calls racing on the same instance' (lines ~224-289). It genuinely races two Task.async/Task.await_many Engine.complete_task/3 calls on two distinct task_ids of the same instance over real separate Postgres connections (TenantFixture's provisioned_tenant!/1 sets sandbox :auto, not :manual, per the test's own comment at line ~236), and asserts both calls succeed ({:ok, _} for both branches), exactly one observes instance_status: :completed and the other :active, and the final instance_projections row's join_counters is %{} (fired and deleted cleanly, not a lost-update partial entry) -- this is the exact cross-call join scenario the original defect broke, and the assertions genuinely test it, not a restated pre-fix expectation.

(2) create/2 extension: read the real lib/letflow/engine.ex code directly, not just ELIXIR-DEV's handoff prose. persist/12's Multi calls insert_instance_projection/8 (defp around line 1166), whose attrs map includes `join_counters: SnapshotWriter.serialize_join_counters(join_counters)`, and the caller at line ~965 passes `new_instance_state.join_counters` -- confirming the fix threads the freshly-dispatched state's own join_counters through create/2's own M1 insert, not just reconcile_projection/5's later updates. Read the real test/letflow/iss0397_join_counters_test.exs 'serial cross-call join' describe block (lines 150-175): `projection_after_create = Repo.get!(InstanceProjection, instance_id, ...)` is asserted `status == :active` and its sole join cohort has `expected_from_branches` length 2 and `received_from_branches == []` -- read directly after Engine.create/2 alone, before either complete_task/3 call runs. This genuinely disproves the pre-fix map_size(join_counters) == 0 defect at the create/2 write site specifically, confirming the extension is shipped and tested, not just mentioned in a handoff.

(3) Pre-existing failures: ran `git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat -- test/letflow/secrets_test.exs test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_toolchain_test.exs` myself -- empty output, confirming neither file appears anywhere in this branch's diff against origin/main. Cross-checked against the full `git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat` (23 files: migration, engine.ex, snapshot_writer.ex, instance_projection.ex, tenant_provisioning.ex, 4 new/changed test files, design doc, anti-patterns.md, handoff/registry bookkeeping) -- neither flagged file is present. Confirms TEST-RUNNER's triage (2 rustc-ENOENT toolchain tests, 1 SecretsTest StreamData property flake) is genuinely unrelated to this branch's changes.

(4) REQ-052 coordination note: read lib/letflow/design/req052-instance-cancellation.md's own §4 and OQ-2 (RESOLVED 2026-08-22, GH#326) directly. It explicitly cites 'the join-counters persistence gap req048's own OQ-3 already discloses' (line 608, also referenced at lines 285-294) as the stated reason cancel_instance/3 does not drive {:cancel_branch, branch_id} through Transition. That cited blocker (join_counters never persisted, always %{}) is now genuinely gone -- confirmed by (1) and (2) above: join_counters is durably persisted on instance_projections and correctly read back on every write/read path (reconcile_projection/5, build_instance_state/3, and now insert_instance_projection/8). ELIXIR-DEV correctly did NOT touch cancel_instance/3 itself (flagged in step-03-elixir-dev.json's routing as 'a decision-record-drift flag for ORCH, not something ELIXIR-DEV resolved unilaterally') -- confirmed this is the right disposition: wiring {:cancel_branch, _} through cancel_instance/3 is real, scoped design work (how to reconstruct a cancellation-scoped join_counters view) that does not belong bundled into a join-counters-persistence bugfix. The note was correctly left as a flag, not silently resolved, and is now genuinely stale as a blocker citation.

(5) Updated docs/issues/ISS-0397.yaml to status: resolved with resolved_in_run: WF03-ISS0397-20260901, resolved_at, and a full resolution: field (following ISS-0380/ISS-0381/ISS-0398's own convention) summarizing the shipped fix (persisted join_counters column + read/write site changes), the create/2 in-family extension found and fixed along the way, the 3 pre-existing/unrelated test failures, and the REQ-052/cancel_instance/3 staleness note as a named follow-on for a future session.

Not blocking this close.
